58|receipt_root=$pool/.provisioning

93|    mkdir -p "$root_mount" "$upgrade_mount"
94|    blockdev --setro "$seed_device"
95|    seed_loop=$(losetup --find --show --read-only "$seed_device")
96|    disk_loop=$(losetup --find --show --partscan "$image")
97|    root_partition=${disk_loop}p1 upgrade_partition=${disk_loop}p2
98|    jq --arg seed "$seed_device" --arg sf "$seed_fsid" --arg sl "$seed_loop" --arg dl "$disk_loop" \
99|        --arg rp "$root_partition" --arg up "$upgrade_partition" --arg rm "$root_mount" --arg um "$upgrade_mount" \
100|        '.seed_device=$seed|.seed_fsid=$sf|.seed_loop=$sl|.disk_loop=$dl|
101|         .root_partition=$rp|.upgrade_partition=$up|.root_mount=$rm|.upgrade_mount=$um' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
102|    mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
103|    for partition in "$root_partition" "$upgrade_partition"; do
104|        [[ -b $partition && -z $(blkid -p -s TYPE -o value "$partition" || true) ]] || fail 'partition is not blank'
105|    done
106|    mount -o ro,subvolid=5 "$seed_loop" "$root_mount"
107|    for member in @ @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_shared @agent_skills @agent_soul @agent_user; do
108|        btrfs subvolume show "$root_mount/$member" >/dev/null || fail "seed missing $member"
109|    done
110|    phase root-device-add-intent
111|    btrfs device add "$root_partition" "$root_mount"
112|    sync -f "$root_mount"
113|    umount "$root_mount"
114|    mount -o "rw,subvolid=5,device=$seed_loop,device=$root_partition" "$root_partition" "$root_mount"
115|    phase upgrade-format-intent
116|    mkfs.btrfs -L 3tched-upgrade "$upgrade_partition"
117|    mount -o rw,subvolid=5 "$upgrade_partition" "$upgrade_mount"
118|    btrfs subvolume create "$upgrade_mount/@"
119|    for member in @agent_memory @agent_rules @agent_skills @agent_user; do
120|        btrfs property set -ts "$root_mount/$member" ro false
121|    done
122|    for member in @agent_shared @agent_soul; do
123|        btrfs property set -ts "$root_mount/$member" ro true
124|    done
125|    install -d -m 0700 "$root_mount/@agent_user/persist"
126|    install -d -m 0755 "$root_mount/@/opt/run-mounts/persist"
127|    sync -f "$root_mount"
128|    sync -f "$upgrade_mount"
129|    jq --arg rf "$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$root_partition")" \
130|        --arg uf "$(blkid -p -s UUID -o value "$upgrade_partition")" \
131|        '.root_fsid=$rf|.upgrade_fsid=$uf|.filesystem_prepared=true|.phase="filesystems-prepared"' "$receipt" > "$receipt.new"
132|    mv -T "$receipt.new" "$receipt"
133|    sync -f "$receipt_root"
134|    printf 'Filesystems prepared; mounts retained for next manual step. Receipt: %s\n' "$receipt"
135|    exit 0
136|fi
137|[[ ! -e $image && ! -L $image ]] || fail 'image already exists; use inspect, never repeat creation'
138|receipt=$receipt_root/$name.json
139|[[ ! -e $receipt && ! -L $receipt ]] || fail 'retained preparation intent exists; inspect before any retry'
140|total_gib=$((root_gib + upgrade_gib))
141|created_at=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
142|jq -n --arg name "$name" --arg image "$image" --arg pool "$pool" --arg time "$created_at" \
143|    --argjson root "$root_gib" --argjson upgrade "$upgrade_gib" --argjson total "$total_gib" \
144|    '{version:1,layout:"raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1",phase:"disk-create-intent",
145|      name:$name,image:$image,pool:$pool,created_at:$time,
146|      root_gib:$root,upgrade_gib_requested:$upgrade,total_gib:$total,
147|      identity_registered:false,filesystem_prepared:false}' > "$receipt"
148|# qemu-img creates a sparse raw disk; GPT/alignment overhead reduces partition 2
149|# slightly. All commands address only the newly created image, never a host disk.
150|qemu-img create -f raw "$image" "${total_gib}G"
151|chmod 0600 "$image"
152|sfdisk "$image" <<PARTITIONS
153|label: gpt
154|unit: sectors
155|
156|size=${root_gib}G, type=L, name="3tched-root"
157|type=L, name="3tched-upgrade"
158|PARTITIONS
159|partition_table=$(sfdisk --json "$image")
160|# Pin partition identities now; loop numbers are runtime attachments, not owners.
161|jq --arg inode "$(stat -c %i "$image")" --argjson bytes "$(stat -c %s "$image")" \

{"content":"1|#!/bin/sh
2|# Mount physical-seed roots after Incus API readiness, then start only ready
3|# session instances (including the fixed chatbot alias). Staging names remain
4|# stopped. This is storage
5|# readiness, without a bridge/lungs dependency. A service restart observes
6|# running instances without stopping them; finish never detaches their roots.
7|exec 2>&1
8|rm -f /run/opdbus/runit-ready/identity-roots
9|
10|wait_dep() {
11|    sv start "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
12|    i=0
13|    until sv check "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; do
14|        i=$((i + 1))
15|        [ "$i" -ge 90 ] && { echo "dependency $1 not ready after 90s" >&2; exit 1; }
16|        sleep 1
17|    done
18|}
19|
20|wait_dep incus
21|
22|i=0
23|until incus info >/dev/null 2>&1; do
24|    i=$((i + 1))
25|    if [ "$i" -ge 60 ]; then
26|        echo "incusd API not ready" >&2
27|        exit 1
28|    fi
29|    sleep 1
30|done
31|
32|helper=/usr/local/libexec/3tched/op-identity-root
33|gpt=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/.provisioning/3tchedChatbot.boot.json
34|if [ -e "$gpt" ] || [ -L "$gpt" ]; then
35|    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/restore-chatbot-root || exit 1
36|    /usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots
37|    exec sleep infinity
38|fi
39|physical=${OP_IDENTITY_SEED_STATE:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/seed-identities}
40|legacy=${IDENTITIES:-/var/lib/opdbus-runtime/identities}
41|physical_present=0
42|seed_readonly_ready=0
43|failed=0
44|for receipt in "$physical"/*/state.json; do
45|    [ -e "$receipt" ] || [ -L "$receipt" ] || continue
46|    physical_present=1
47|    name=$(basename "$(dirname "$receipt")")
48|    if [ "$name" != 3tchedChatbot ] && ! printf '%s' "$name" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
49|        echo "physical seed staging receipt $name: boot disabled"
50|        continue
51|    fi
52|    marker="$physical/$name/boot-ready.json"
53|    if [ ! -e "$marker" ] && [ ! -L "$marker" ]; then
54|        echo "physical seed $name: no authoritative-completion boot opt-in; skipped"
55|        continue
56|    fi
57|    # A canonical name alone does not prove provisioning completed. The helper
58|    # checks the owner attestation marker and all storage/native identity pins.
59|    if ! jq -e --arg name "$name" '
60|        .name == $name and .phase == "ready" and
61|        (.session == $name or ($name == "3tchedChatbot" and .session == "b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28"))
62|    ' "$receipt" >/dev/null; then
63|        echo "physical seed $name: invalid/incomplete receipt; legacy suppressed" >&2
64|        failed=$((failed + 1))
65|        continue
66|    fi
67|    start_on_boot=$(jq -er '.start_on_boot | select(type == "boolean") | tostring' "$marker") || {
68|        echo "physical seed $name: invalid boot completion policy" >&2
69|        failed=$((failed + 1))
70|        continue
71|    }
72|    # The physical partition's kernel RO flag is volatile across reboot.
73|    # The host owner restores it once, after ready/opt-in selection and before
74|    # any seed-check/up; verification failures stop boot restoration closed.
75|    if [ "$seed_readonly_ready" -eq 0 ]; then
76|        "$helper" seed-readonly || { echo "physical seed read-only enforcement failed" >&2; exit 1; }
77|        seed_readonly_ready=1
78|    fi
79|    state=$(incus query "/1.0/instances/$name/state" | jq -er '.status') || state=unknown
80|    case "$state" in
81|        Running)
82|            if "$helper" seed-check "$name"; then
83|                "$helper" seed-lungs "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
84|            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
85|            ;;
86|        Stopped)
87|            if "$helper" seed-up "$name" && "$helper" seed-lungs "$name"; then
88|                if [ "$start_on_boot" = true ]; then incus start "$name" || failed=$((failed + 1))
89|                else echo "physical seed $name: storage restored; boot start disabled"; fi
90|            else failed=$((failed + 1)); fi
91|            ;;
92|        *) echo "physical seed $name: unsupported native status $state" >&2
93|            failed=$((failed + 1)) ;;
94|    esac
95|done
96|if [ "$physical_present" -eq 1 ]; then
97|    # A direct legacy lower mount conflicts with sprouts from the SAME seed,
98|    # even for a different identity. Do not invoke legacy `up` in this mode.
99|    for image in "$legacy"/*/identity.img; do
100|        [ -f "$image" ] || continue
101|        name=$(basename "$(dirname "$image")")
102|        if [ -e "$physical/$name/state.json" ] || [ -L "$physical/$name/state.json" ]; then
103|            echo "legacy identity $name: suppressed by physical seed receipt"
104|        else
105|            echo "legacy identity $name: migration or independent lower required; shared seed direct mount suppressed" >&2
106|            failed=$((failed + 1))
107|        fi
108|    done
109|else
110|    "$helper" up || failed=$((failed + 1))
111|    "$helper" status || failed=$((failed + 1))
112|fi
113|[ "$failed" -eq 0 ] || { echo "$failed identity root startup check(s) failed" >&2; exit 1; }
114|/usr/local/libexec/3tched/runit-ready-signal identity-roots

{"content":"1|# Shared physical seed and private leaves
2|
3|## Manual provisioning checkpoint: partitioned instance disk
4|
5|The October 11 manual workflow uses a sparse QEMU raw image under
6|`/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool`, mounted from `@3tched-leaf-pool` on the host's
7|main Btrfs pool. This subvolume isolates the storage path, but shares that
8|pool's capacity. The shared seed remains the separate sealed 20 GiB partition;
9|no instance identity or Cozo binding is written into it.
10|
11|The completed image preparation step is available through the provisioner:
12|
13|```sh
14|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
15|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
16|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-filesystems 3tchedChatbot \
17|  --seed-device /dev/disk/by-uuid/3415d575-7224-4484-9e0d-06854ac5f032
18|```
19|
20|Preparation creates a 60 GiB sparse raw image with GPT: 20 GiB root and the
21|remaining approximately 40 GiB upgrade partition. `--root-gib` and
22|`--upgrade-gib` select capacities on a new image. The upgrade remainder is
23|slightly smaller than its requested capacity because GPT and alignment consume
24|space. The image and a private preparation receipt live in the leaf pool;
25|the receipt pins the image inode and both partition identities. An interrupted
26|creation retains its intent and image instead of retrying or cleaning them up.
27|`inspect` does not register or adopt an existing image.
28|
29|The filesystem stage attaches a read-only loop view of the sealed seed and adds
30|the blank root partition once as its writable leaf. It inherits the seven seed
31|subvolumes; it does not copy the root or create replacement agent subvolumes.
32|Only the upgrade partition is formatted, with one `@` subvolume. Shared and soul
33|are read-only in the leaf; memory, rules, skills and user are writable. Private
34|persistence directories are ordinary directories. Both mounts stay attached for
35|the next manual step. The receipt records loops, mounts and fresh filesystem
36|UUIDs. Interrupted intents require investigation, and prepared receipts cannot
37|repeat device-add or formatting. Never modify the seed after leaves depend on it.
38|
39|Neither stage performs seed transport, Incus creation, identity registration or
40|startup. They have no identity/backend preflight dependency.
41|Those later steps remain subject to the owner's manual
42|script comparison. The existing identity mode described below expects an
43|unpartitioned leaf and must not be used with this new partitioned image.
44|
45|The upgrade lifecycle is host → container only, using Btrfs without Unison:
46|
47|```sh
48|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
49|sudo ./deploy/scripts/provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
50|```
51|
52|Pairing sends a read-only snapshot of host upgrade `/dev/sdc3` (`@`) to
53|partition 2 during provisioning, including when the first upgrade is empty.
54|Subsequent synchronization sends incrementally from the retained
55|common baseline, including deletions within the upgrade tree. Received baselines stay read-only;
56|the published upgrade `@` is a writable clone. Transfer intents and prior
57|versions are retained for recovery; interrupted publication is not retried
58|automatically. Snapshot retention cleanup is not implemented by this stage.
59|
60|The chatbot runit startup invokes `boot` for explicitly paired storage before
61|starting the container. It restores existing loop/mount attachments, synchronizes,
62|then publishes a read-only OverlayFS OS view at `.mounts/NAME/root-view`.
63|The upgrade layer takes precedence over the seed-root layer; an empty upgrade
64|uses the installed seed. Patches removing seed files must include OverlayFS
65|whiteouts: deleting a file from the upgrade tree alone reveals its seed copy.
66|The Btrfs layers receive the container UID mapping before mounting OverlayFS,
67|because this kernel rejects mapping the merged overlay. The view is bound at
68|the Incus-managed `identity-roots` rootfs, preserving its pool definition.
69|Six agent subvolumes are separately bound into `/agent`; their existing writable
70|or read-only policies remain in effect, with private persistence bound separately.
71|User contents are never sent or received. Synchronization detaches stopped OS
72|views before rotating a lower layer; it never changes Btrfs membership.
73|This new image is not yet admitted by the older unpartitioned root-owner lifecycle;
74|its identity-root integration remains part of the subsequent provisioning step.
75|
76|The seed has the seven sibling subvolumes and guest systemd FUSE service.
77|`@agent_rules/rules/rules.md` and `@agent_user/user/user.md` are initial
78|per-instance documents: their content is changed in each private writable leaf,
79|not in the sealed seed. Shared owner links expose cognitive memory, skills,
80|routing and plugins without granting authority or starting those features.
81|
82|## Earlier unpartitioned-leaf integration
83|
84|The following describes the earlier helper contract. Its device paths,
85|host-owned FUSE attachment and early backend gates are not the new manual
86|partitioned-disk workflow and still require reconciliation before automation.
87|
88|Identity provisioning uses one immutable Btrfs seed on the physical partition
89|currently named `/dev/sdb2`. Each container has its own writable leaf. A leaf
90|stores that container's changes; it does not contain a copied root filesystem.
91|Golden preparation includes the wrapper and its helpers under `libexec/3tched`;
92|after release activation, the operator entrypoint is
93|`/usr/local/libexec/3tched/provision-workspace-subscriber`.
94|
95|The seed's top-level layout is `@`, `@agent_memory`, `@agent_rules`,
96|`@agent_shared`, `@agent_skills`, `@agent_soul`, and `@agent_user`. Provisioning
97|uses these existing subvolumes in the sprout. It does not create snapshots,
98|send/receive root filesystems, copy seed images, or use an overlay root.
99|Readonly loop views reference the same physical partition bytes.
100|
101|`provision-workspace-subscriber.sh` first verifies the mounted operator
102|3tchedFS session and sealed catalog, then calls the declared identity inventory
103|and provisioning preflight operations through their `call` files. It checks
104|the operation receipts before invoking the read-only
105|`op-identity-root seed-preflight`, followed by `seed-profile`, before creating
106|an empty Incus instance with the `3tched-lungs` profile.
107|The helper checks the physical seed identity, SEEDING flag and block read-only
108|state, and refuses a direct mount of the physical source. The wrapper holds
109|a per-session lock; the helper serializes seed loop setup and leaf creation.
110|`seed-create` adds the new private writable leaf once. Later starts mount
111|that existing leaf; stopping does not remove a Btrfs member. Failed starts
112|also retain membership. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage;
113|its `attached` field describes logical attachment, not device membership.
114|The session hostname and private persistence are
115|created through the sprout, so those writes belong to the leaf. Persistence is
116|an ordinary mode-0700 directory at `@agent_user/persist`, bound to the guest's
117|`/opt/run-mounts/persist`. Provisioning creates no subvolumes at all: only the
118|seven inherited members are used. Agent soul,
119|and shared subvolumes remain protected in the guest view. Rules and user
120|preferences are instance-specific and writable in each private leaf.
121|
122|Storage receipts identify this layout as `shared-partition-siblings-v2` and
123|pin its inherited subvolume identities plus the persistence directory's inode,
124|parent subvolume identity, sprout FSID and image metadata digest. The directory must remain on its
125|parent filesystem and cannot be a symlink, separate mount, or subvolume.
126|Older v1 receipts with an extra `@persist` subvolume and snapshot-based receipts are
127|rejected; this change does not silently migrate them or replace existing
128|container roots. Existing live persistence and older containers are neither
129|deleted nor converted; replacement must be prepared separately. Historical
130|soul reconciliation now verifies existing subvolumes and native devices only,
131|and fails when they are missing instead of creating them.
132|
133|Before sealing a new base, `op-identity-image prepare TOP RELEASE_ID
134|PROVENANCE_JSON` records the archive provenance, offline package inventory,
135|critical file hashes and exact seven-member layout. It also prepares ordinary
136|mountpoint directories under `@/run/mount/3tchedFS` and `@/run/opdbus/lungs`.
137|The helper does not download or verify the archive signature, mount storage,
138|toggle SEEDING, format devices or create subvolumes. See
139|[image preparation](../../../deploy/workspace-image/README.md) for its input
140|contract. Creation fully verifies the pristine image before adding a leaf;
141|later checks verify the pinned metadata without rejecting legitimate private
142|package updates in the leaf.
143|
144|FUSE runs on the host. Fresh provisioning selects a persistent Incus `disk`
145|device named `3tched`, exposing the session's own host FUSE mount at
146|`/run/mount/3tchedFS`. The seed needs an empty destination directory, not a
147|guest FUSE daemon. A native instance UUID pins the host source and process
148|receipt. An existing legacy hook receipt is verified without silently
149|converting its attachment mechanism. The common `/etc/3tched` directories
150|are a separate read-only Incus disk attachment, with links from the inherited
151|agent subvolumes.
152|
153|The `3tched-lungs` Incus profile supplies these inherited devices:
154|
155|```yaml
156|config: {}
157|devices:
158|  runtime-run:
159|    type: disk
160|    source: "tmpfs:"
161|    path: /run
162|    initial.mode: "0755"
163|  lungs-socket-dir:
164|    type: disk
165|    source: /run/opdbus/lungs
166|    path: /run/opdbus/lungs
167|    readonly: "true"
168|```
169|
170|The bridge service creates its existing shared socket at
171|`/run/opdbus/lungs/lungs.sock`. Mounting its dedicated parent directory keeps
172|socket replacement visible to each guest without exposing other host runtime
173|files. `seed-profile` creates this exact profile if absent and rejects existing
174|configuration drift. Provisioning also verifies the inherited devices and
175|rejects local overrides. The `/run` tmpfs is mounted before its child devices;
176|image directories alone would not establish that boot ordering.
177|
178|The bridge creates a root-owned socket with mode 0666 beneath the root-owned
179|0755 directory. Connection permission allows negotiation; each operation still
180|requires an authenticated identity and its existing capability grant. Host
181|`Bind(session)` requires UID 0 in the bridge's own user and PID namespaces.
182|Guest `BindCurrentContainer()` takes no session argument: it pins the socket's
183|original process with SO_PEERPIDFD and derives identity from the exact running
184|native container. Process, native UUID and authoritative identity are checked
185|again for each call. No SID1 file is installed in the guest.
186|
187|Clean replacement is scoped to the configured chatbot key and service identity
188|`b0c777e3-0955-cd8b-3d01-ca12998cae28`, using the provisioner's configured native
189|alias `3tchedCtlbot`. Hostname remains the session UUID. The old native instance
190|must be stopped or authoritatively absent, and the new name and leaf must be
191|unused. Explicit retirement uses `identity_sled.delete_provision_record` through
192|the operator's mounted namespace, with the existing human write capability
193|and exact revision. This removes the current row and retains an audit tombstone;
194|startup respects that tombstone. A version3 plan permits fresh provisioning
195|from that exact deletion receipt. Ordinary missing rows are not accepted.
196|After host storage/mount
197|preparation, the wrapper submits a digest-pinned private plan through the
198|supported `identity_sled.provision_container` operation. The owner atomically
199|creates fresh current-schema state and binds it to the new native instance;
200|legacy persistence and record fields are not imported. Existing external
201|capability policy remains in force. Normal provisioning starts through
202|`touch_session`; `--no-start` leaves the fresh identity parked. Only verified
203|completion receives a boot-ready marker.
204|
205|If creation fails, `op-identity-root seed-inspect NAME` reports sanitized
206|receipt metadata and recovery guidance without mounting, formatting or
207|retrying device-add. Preserve the receipt, base, leaf and mappings until the
208|recorded intent and actual membership have been reconciled.
209|
210|Preparing or changing the live seed is a separate operator action. The helper
211|does not set or clear SEEDING, format the partition, or unmount an unrelated
212|source mount. Once leaves depend on a seed, that seed must remain unchanged.
213|At boot, the host storage service uses `seed-readonly` to verify the physical
214|partition identity and existing SEEDING state, then restore its volatile block
215|read-only flag before restoring opted-in roots. This never changes filesystem
216|membership or the SEEDING flag.
217|The current source change has not been deployed or validated with concurrent
218|live containers on the fresh base. The September 30 file-backed and physical
219|seed experiments did demonstrate independent writes, peer-active remounts and
220|cold loop recreation using distinct read-only views of the same seed on this
221|kernel. That evidence does not validate this new image/layout or a full host
222|reboot. There is no fallback to copied seeds if a kernel rejects the shared
223|arrangement. The owner's current sequencing instruction defers all tests until
224|after deployment; a successful build alone is not a workflow validation.
225|
226|See the [Btrfs seeding documentation](https://btrfs.readthedocs.io/en/latest/Seeding-device.html).","total_lines":226,"file_size":13507,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}

{"content":"1|#!/usr/bin/env bash
2|# Provision a fresh shared root for the EXISTING configured chatbot key.
3|# Completed manual storage stage (no identity/backend preflight):
4|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-disk 3tchedChatbot
5|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --inspect-disk 3tchedChatbot
6|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot
7|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --pair-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
8|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --bind-root 3tchedChatbot
9|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --prepare-adoption 3tchedChatbot
10|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --sync-upgrade 3tchedChatbot
11|#     [--root-gib 20 --upgrade-gib 40]   # prepare-disk only
12|# Creates /var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool/NAME.img: raw GPT root + upgrade.
13|# --prepare-container defines the stopped chatbot and socket profile only;
14|# it does not bind the prepared root, adopt the identity or start the guest.
15|# This stage ends before formatting, seed attachment, Incus creation or Cozo
16|# registration. Existing identity mode below remains the older unpartitioned
17|# leaf workflow; do not pass a partitioned image to that mode.
18|# Usage:
19|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh LABEL --session-id UUID --pubkey B64 \
20|#     --operator-session UUID --leaf-path ABSOLUTE_PATH --principal-group '$ROOT' \
21|#     [--fstorage-gib N] [--no-start]
22|#     [--container-name 3tchedChatbot]   # configured chatbot key only
23|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh NAME --system \
24|#     [--image ALIAS|FINGERPRINT] [--storage POOL] [--no-start]
25|#   sudo ./provision-workspace-subscriber.sh --system NAME [system options]
26|#
27|# Identity mode never signs up an account, generates/copies credentials,
28|# deletes/recreates a container, or attaches a leaf to an Incus filesystem.
29|# Clean replacement is currently scoped to the configured chatbot alias
30|# 3tchedChatbot. LABEL is display metadata, never authority.
31|# Existing native names and storage receipts are refused.
32|# --no-start prepares storage, reconciles and verifies attach, leaving STOPPED.
33|# The old native instance must be stopped. The supported owner operation
34|# creates a fresh parked current-schema record using the same key and SID;
35|# supported touch then starts it after attached readback. --no-start leaves
36|# the new identity parked. Credential bytes are not requested or inspected;
37|# supported method results redact them. This wrapper never mints credentials.
38|# Completion enables root/FUSE restoration on boot; --no-start records a
39|# stopped boot policy. Incomplete storage never receives a boot-ready marker.
40|# The physical seed is one immutable filesystem shared by all leaves. Storage
41|# preparation uses its existing seven subvolumes through a private writable
42|# sprout; it never snapshots, copies, sends or receives a container root.
43|# Each guest gets its session ID as /etc/hostname and the LXC UTS hostname.
44|# seed-lungs configures the persistent Incus disk attaching the identity's own
45|# host FUSE mount at /run/mount/3tchedFS on every start.
46|# The 3tched-lungs profile provides /run tmpfs and the dedicated host socket
47|# directory at the same /run/opdbus/lungs path inside each new container.
48|# Failures retain native/storage intent and private sanitized receipts.
49|# Host helper/catalog defaults select activated release artifacts.
50|# Selected overrides must be root-controlled. This is host operator maintenance,
51|# not a guest-accessible host socket or a new identity minting authority.
52|# --system remains ordinary Raccoon cloud provisioning without identity changes.
53|set -euo pipefail
54|die() { printf 'ERROR: %s\n' "$*" >&2; exit 1; }
55|need_cmd() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing command: $1"; }
56|usage() { sed -n '2,20p' "$0"; }
57|if [[ $# == 0 || ${1:-} == -h || ${1:-} == --help ]]; then usage; exit 0; fi
58|prepare_chatbot_container() (
59|    # Host preparation only: no identity adoption, root copy, device-add or start.
60|    [[ $# == 1 && $1 == 3tchedChatbot ]] || die 'usage: --prepare-container 3tchedChatbot'
61|    [[ $(id -u) == 0 ]] || die 'container preparation requires host root'
62|    for tool in incus jq findmnt stat flock realpath sync; do need_cmd "$tool"; done
63|    incus() { command incus --force-local "$@"; }
64|    umask 077
65|    pool_root=/var/lib/3tched-leaf-pool
66|    receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.json
67|    container_receipt=$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.incus.json
68|    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M "$pool_root" -o FSROOT) == /@3tched-leaf-pool &&
69|       -f $receipt && ! -L $receipt && ! -e $container_receipt && ! -L $container_receipt ]] ||
70|        die 'prepared disk receipt required; existing container intents must be reconciled manually'
71|    jq -e --arg name "$1" '.name==$name and .phase=="filesystems-prepared" and
72|        .layout=="raw-gpt-root-upgrade-v1" and .filesystem_prepared==true and .identity_registered==false' \
73|        "$receipt" >/dev/null || die 'disk is not ready for container definition'
74|    image=$(jq -er .image "$receipt")
75|    [[ $image == "$pool_root/$1.img" && -f $image && ! -L $image &&
76|       $(stat -c %i "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_inode "$receipt")" &&
77|       $(stat -c %s "$image") == "$(jq -r .image_bytes "$receipt")" ]] || die 'prepared image changed'
78|    exec 9>"$pool_root/.provisioning/$1.lock"
79|    flock -n 9 || die 'instance preparation active'
80|    instances=$(incus list -f json)
81|    jq -e --arg name "$1" 'type=="array" and all(.[]; .name!=$name)' <<<"$instances" >/dev/null ||
82|        die 'container already exists; never recreate it'
83|    [[ $(findmnt -rn -M /var/lib/incus-storage -o FSROOT) == /@incus ]] || die 'Incus subvolume not mounted'
84|    pool_source=/var/lib/incus-storage/identity-roots
85|    pools=$(incus storage list -f json)

87|        pool_json=$(incus query /1.0/storage-pools/identity-roots)

{"content":"1|# Network Operations
2|
3|This page describes **how networking is supposed to work on the current Artix/runit host**, and points at the live inventory when the tree and the machine disagree.
4|
5|For a dated, command-verified snapshot of interfaces, Incus devices, listeners, xray SNI, and mesh forwarders, see:
6|
7|**[Host socket & network topology (live)](host-socket-topology-live.md)**
8|
9|Re-verify that file against the host before topology-changing work (new proxies, prom/graf exposure, socket migrations).
10|
11|## Agent rules and owner decisions (moved from AGENTS.md, 2026-10-14)
12|
13|Read this section before any network, Xray, WARP, decoy, OVS or firewall work.
14|AGENTS.md now only points here.
15|
16|**Partial restoration (2026-10-16).** The native `decoy-admin-reverse-ssh`
17|runit service is restored on the Devuan host using the existing
18|`/home/jeremy/.ssh/decoy_key` and strict host-key checking. The decoy publishes
19|`10.0.0.1:2222` bound to `wg-opdbus`, forwarding to its loopback reverse endpoint;
20|the tunnel terminates at the host's loopback SSH listener. WireGuard terminates
21|only on the decoy, never on this host. A fresh authenticated reverse connection
22|returned `jeremy` on `3tched` and matched the host's authoritative ED25519 key.
23|The external WireGuard-client leg was not exercised from this session.
24|
25|The target layout is eth0 as OVS uplink, pub0 for public addressing (not
26|administrative SSH), two IPv4 addresses on `rtly-lungs` including 10.0.0.2,
27|and three service aliases on ovsbr0 for EMQX, OpenFlow and Qdrant. OVS packages
28|are installed, but no bridge/address/route ownership cutover has occurred.
29|NetworkManager remains active until a protected transfer; afterward it must
30|remain installed but disabled, for emergency recovery only.
31|
32|Owner requests stopping at the application-bridge prerequisite. The existing
33|uplink service waits for `opdbus-rundirs`, which requires `/usr/local/bin/opblob`
34|and a prepared persisted catalog; that executable is absent. This is an
35|application-catalog bootstrap dependency, not proof that the bridge daemon must
36|run to create OVS. Do not bypass it or claim the network cutover is deployed.
37|Public recovery SSH is still enabled: a proposed private-only cutover was
38|reverted when its rollback helper could not execute on the `noexec` `/run`
39|mount. Move forward only with an approved, functioning rollback mechanism.
40|
41|**Current status (2026-10-14).** The host moved from Artix to Devuan 6 (runit:
42|`/etc/sv/<svc>`, enabled via `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`). Only `eth0`
43|(`188.68.58.237/22`, DHCP) is up; OVS, Incus, Xray and WARP are not installed yet.
44|Owner decision: the network lives on the **base system**, not in a golden release,
45|installed on a new machine by a network preinstall script that pulls these
46|sources from git. The rest of this page, including the GRE description below,
47|predates that move: GRE (`gre-decoy`) and `wgcf` were retired on 2026-10-04 (see
48|`deploy/runit/retired-services`), and `deploy/config/nftables.conf` says SSH
49|transport now uses `tun5`. Xray config/keys and the Xray Incus container are not
50|in git; the recovery disk keeps them under `received/271/root-271/`
51|(`etc/xray`, `var/lib/incus`, `etc/openvswitch`, `etc/nftables.conf`).
52|
53|**Network-critical services.** OVS, uplink, DHCP and the session bus require
54|deliberate operator action; a learning or inventory pass never restarts them.
55|
56|**Xray configuration policy — mandatory.** Xray's live config must exist only at
57|`/etc/xray/xray_config.json` inside the container. Never point Xray at
58|`/dev/shm/xray_config.json`, `/usr/local/etc/xray/config.json`, or any other
59|disk-backed live path. The static bootstrap config is materialized at boot; the
60|future model-generated generator replaces the same file atomically and reloads
61|through D-Bus. Models must not write or reload Xray directly.
62|
63|**Owner-confirmed network topology (2026-09-13).** There is no WireGuard on this
64|server. WireGuard terminates at the decoy; identity is transported by WARP.
65|WireGuard types, plugin declarations, credentials or historical configuration
66|paths in source do not establish a server WireGuard interface or a requirement to
67|install one. Classify those surfaces by their decoy/server role before proposing
68|implementation or retirement. An unwired `wgcf` method is not evidence that the
69|actual WARP identity transport is broken.
70|
71|**Owner decisions: decoy GRE, TLS and identity transport (2026-09-25; GRE since
72|retired).** The door stays `10.0.0.2:8090`: tonic with the internal `svc0`
73|certificate from the op-dbus local CA. The bridge no longer listens on
74|`127.0.0.1:8090` or `10.0.0.3:8090`, and it no longer serves a second browser
75|certificate. Browser-facing TLS terminates on the decoy at `10.0.0.1`. The decoy
76|mints the sealed identity blob, and WARP delivers it to the 8090 interceptor. The
77|oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed proof of the WireGuard peer, because
78|WireGuard exists only on the decoy. At the time, the decoy routed browser
79|traffic for `10.0.0.2` over `gre-host` with no WARP route in either main routing
80|table. The `gre-decoy` tunnel joined decoy and host: outer `188.68.58.237` ↔
81|`129.80.64.127`, inner `192.168.255.1/30` plus `10.0.0.2/32`, with `10.0.0.1` and
82|the WireGuard clients `10.0.0.5`–`10.0.0.7` routed via `192.168.255.2`. GRE
83|routing replaced NAT on that path: nftables is the firewall only, never a router,
84|so do not add DNAT, SNAT or masquerade for it. GRE is not encrypted, so anything
85|crossing it that is not TLS is readable on the path. MQTT stays on `10.0.0.3`,
86|aliased on `ovsbr0` beside the OpenFlow address `10.200.0.1`. Xray runs in its
87|container. op-web's page address is `http://10.0.0.4:8080`: plain HTTP outside
88|the TLS zone, with `10.0.0.4/32` on `gre-decoy` and routed from the decoy over
89|`gre-host`. The decoy issuer
90|(`/etc/systemd/system/op-decoy-issuer.service.d/browser-auth.conf` on the decoy,
91|not in this repo) hands out the IP door `https://10.0.0.2:8090` and allows the
92|`10.0.0.4` and `10.0.0.2` page origins; no domain name points browsers at the
93|decoy. Open on 2026-09-25: how the decoy-minted oracle reaches the interceptor
94|(the owner's direction then was over GRE). Until that lands, the deployed page
95|fetches OIA1 from `http://10.0.0.1:51888/identity/self`, and the door rejects a
96|request that carries no credential.
97|
98|## Model in one paragraph
99|
100|One OVS bridge (`ovsbr0`) carries the private fabric. Physical uplink (`eth0`) is enslaved and unaddressed; host L3 lives on OVS internal ports **`pub0`** (public) and **`svc0`** (`10.200.0.2/24`). The **xray** container is the only instance with a NIC on the bridge (`10.200.0.1`). WireGuard mesh interface **`3tched`** (`100.69.0.254/16`) is separate L3 and must never be routed via `ovsbr0`.
101|
102|**Shared socket fabric:** `op-grpc-bridge` dual-listens on host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` and shared container UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` (same gRPC routes). NIC-less containers bind-mount `/run/ghostbridge`. Some services still use Incus TCP proxies / mesh `fwd-*` (migration is incremental).
103|
104|**OpenFlow** (`op-of-controller` on `127.0.0.1:6653`) is intentionally NORMAL/standalone today — reserved for **future tag routing**, not a current blocker for the socket fabric.
105|
106|## Boot order (runit)
107|
108|```text
109|opdbus-rundirs
110|  → uplink-dhcp
111|  → ovsdb-server → ovs-vswitchd
112|  → ovsbr0-uplink → ovsbr0-addr → ovsbr0-svc-addr
113|  → op-of-controller
114|  → wg-3tched
115|  → op-grpc-bridge (cognitive in process) / op-web
116|```
117|
118|Config: `/etc/op-dbus/network.conf`  
119|Helpers: `/usr/local/libexec/3tched/*-up`
120|
121|## Public path
122|
123|Client DNS (NextDNS) → Oracle decoy → WireGuard mesh → host `fwd-8444` → xray SNI on `10.200.0.1:8444` → host services on `10.200.0.2` (dashboard/registration → `:8080`, assistant gRPC → `:8090`, etc.). Live rules: `/dev/shm/xray_config.json` only.
124|
125|## Attachment modes (summary)
126|
127|| Pattern | Used by (live) |
128|| --- | --- |
129|| Bridged NIC on `ovsbr0` | `xray` only |
130|| Shared UDS `/run/ghostbridge/container.sock` | bridge + CT mounts (`assistant`, `qdrant`) |
131|| Incus `proxy` TCP | `mail-3tched`, `netmaker`, `qdrant`, `cozo` |
132|| Mesh `tcpfwd.py` (`fwd-*`) | side channels into xray/host |
133|| Host UDS `/run/opdbus/grpc.sock` | host gRPC clients, session bus |
134|
135|## Do / don't
136|
137|- **Do** check `sudo incus config device show <name>` before assuming UDS-only or proxy-only.
138|- **Do** keep mesh routes on `3tched`; strip accidental `100.69.0.0/16` via `ovsbr0`.
139|- **Do** treat the [Netmaker ACL helper](host-socket-topology-live.md#break-glass-netmaker-acl-recovery) as break-glass recovery; it enables wildcard all-node traffic and bypasses the normal D-Bus path.
140|- **Do not** put `10.200.0.1` on the host.
141|- **Do not** point live xray at `/etc/xray/config.json`.
142|- **Do not** expose Prometheus/Grafana from the netmaker container until the live topology doc is current and the path (mesh vs SNI vs loopback) is chosen.
143|

For OP-DBUS PluginSchema, generated plugin services, reflection, and seal/freeze/hot work, `grpc-expert` takes precedence over the generic `grpc-protocol-expert`; use the generic skill for protocol, channel, TLS, streaming, and observability concerns. 116|## Host-service policy (runit)
117|
118|This server runs **Artix Linux with glibc**, not Chimera or a musl-based host.
119|Build and test the server for `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`. An installed musl
120|cross target or the Codex executable's own musl packaging does not change the
121|repository's native target. Any separate container portability test must name
122|its target and must not substitute for the Artix/glibc verification gate.
123|
124|This host runs **runit** as PID 1. Manage services with `sudo sv <command> <service>` (e.g., `sudo sv restart op-grpc-bridge`). `sv` needs root to read `supervise/ok`.
125|
126|- `/etc/runit/sv/<service>/run` is the service definition.
127|- Enabled by a symlink in `/etc/runit/runsvdir/default`.
128|- Update path: edit the `run` script or install a new binary, then `sudo sv restart <service>`.
129|
130|Do not edit `/run/runit/service` directly. Do not invoke `runsv`/`runsvdir` by hand. **s6 is legacy**: `service6`, `s6-rc`, `s6-*`, `/run/service` are stale — treat any doc assuming them as historical. Note: `/usr/local/bin/systemctl` on this host is a shim that returns plausible answers — using it masks the deprecation; always use `sv`. Do not use `systemctl` or other foreign service-manager CLIs. Container/app deployment uses D-Bus via `busctl`.
131|
132|## Network
133|
134|Network topology, Xray policy, decoy/WARP transport and network-critical
135|service rules are in `docs/src/operations/network.md`. Read it before any
136|network work; it is not needed otherwise.
137|
138|## Deployment (btrfs send/receive)
139|
140|**Owner clarification (2026-09-13): there is no deployment script. Deployment
141|is btrfs send/receive of the prepared filesystem snapshot.** The release
142|boundary is the snapshot's contents and the send/receive transfer. Existing
143|`deploy/` scripts are source/history or preparation tooling; neither
144|`build-golden.sh` nor `btrfs-layout.sh` defines the current deployment mechanism.
145|Never hand-copy binaries onto a running host as a deploy step.
146|
147|**Owner decision (2026-10-14): `./activate-golden.sh` at the repo root is the one
148|command for deploying a new version.** It runs the internal
149|`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` helper, then `op-release-launch release`:
150|btrfs send/receive of a golden snapshot into the inactive of two slots, then a
151|live read-only overlay swap at `/opt/op-dbus/current` (active + previous only;
152|`op-release-launch rollback` undoes it). The 2026-09-13 "no deployment script"
153|rule above is superseded for this entry point; the transport is still send/receive.
154|
155|`deploy/lib/golden/build-golden.sh` only populates and validates
156|`/opt/op-dbus/golden` from already built artifacts and an already sealed,
157|persisted catalog. Set `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE` to use an isolated release
158|catalog; the script validates and copies it but never reseals it. It does not
159|create the read-only release snapshot, send
160|or receive it, activate a received filesystem, install files into the running
161|host, or restart services. `--golden-only` remains a compatibility alias for
162|its default behavior; the former `--live-only` and `--no-restart` modes are
163|retired. Snapshot creation, `btrfs send/receive`, target activation, and any
164|deliberate target service action are separate operator steps.
165|
166|```sh
167|CXXFLAGS="-include cstdint" cargo build --workspace --release
168|sudo target/release/opblob seal-shm            # explicitly reseal after the build
169|sudo target/release/opblob persist             # retain the catalog across reboot
170|```
171|
172|After builds, explicitly run the freshly built `opblob` to seal the release catalog; bridge startup only consumes sealed blobs and never reseals. For isolated release preparation, use `seal-plugins <new-catalog-dir>` and pass that catalog as `OP_PERSISTED_CATALOG_SOURCE`; publishing live SHM remains part of activation. Match the service's schema-shaping environment. The renamed cognitive code reads `COGNITIVE_*`: `COGNITIVE_QDRANT_URL` defaults to `http://127.0.0.1:6334`, matching the current `deploy/runit/op-grpc-bridge/run`; the historical `COGNITIVE_MCP_QDRANT_URL=http://10.200.0.2:6334` instruction is obsolete. After an explicit GNU-target build, use `target/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/release/opblob`, not an older default-target artifact. Verify the live and persisted catalogs match after activation. Review catalog removals and keep a recoverable copy before a full reseal, which sweeps plugin IDs absent from the build.
173|
174|The commands above describe build/catalog preparation, not deployment. Do not
175|infer a live install or restart from a successful build or snapshot preparation.
176|
177|**Clean-baseline activation (2026-09-22):** local releases are received under
178|`/opt/op-dbus/releases/<release-id>` and selected by the atomic
179|`/opt/op-dbus/current` symlink. The operator procedure and rollback contract
180|are in `docs/src/getting-started/local-release-activation.md`. Executable and
181|selected configuration paths link into the received read-only tree; writable
182|service supervision, credentials and runtime data stay outside it. The
183|`tched-router` runit service owns the pinned threetched executable on loopback
184|8084; the duplicate `zeroclaw` service name is retired. This defines the
185|previously missing activation contract, not a new deployment script.
186|
187|## Workspace shape and build
188|
189|The workspace has **37 member crates under `crates/`, plus the root `op-dbus`
190|package** (38 workspace packages total). The root package has no application
191|binary. Binary targets live in members: for example `op-grpc-bridge` and
192|`op-grants-materializer` in `op-grpc-bridge`, `op-web-server` and `opdbus` in
193|`op-web`, `opblob` in `op-plugins`, `3tched-fs` (our 3tchedFS schema filesystem,
194|package `tched-fs`, Rust 2024 edition) in the retained `crates/threetched-fs` directory, and `op-runit-systemctl`/`svd` in
195|`op-runit-systemctl`. A binary target or runit directory is source inventory,
196|not proof that it is deployed; reconcile it with `enabled-services` and
197|`retired-services`. There is no `op-projection` crate. `[patch.crates-io]`
198|patches only `rovs-openflow` (vendored fork for OF1.5 `packet_type` match at
199|`vendor/rovs-openflow`). `op-ml`, `op-gallery-gen`, and `op-uds-relay` have manifests under `crates/`
200|but are outside workspace membership; `op-ml` remains disabled for the ort API breakage (`#ml-fixme`).
201|
202|**Rust-first: no new Python.** New automation, probes, and helpers go in Rust (`cargo run --bin <name> -p <crate> -- <args>`, a small binary in the relevant crate, or a `cargo-script`-style one-shot) or in shell + POSIX tools (`jq`, `curl`, `busctl`, `sv`). Do not add new `.py` files to the repo. Pre-existing scripts under `scripts/` (`export-llm-sessions-to-notebooklm-sources.py`, `or-fusion-archive.py`, `notebook-sources-cleanup.py`, etc.) are grandfathered — maintain them in place, don't propagate the pattern.
203|
204|**Skill runtime tools may be run directly (owner, 2026-10-14).** The tools that back the skills installed by `install_3tched_skills.sh` — `zero`, `bd`/`bv` (beads), `trestle` (Compliance Trestle), and the Hugging Face stack (`hf`, `trl`, `trackio`, `transformers`, `sentence-transformers`, `datasets`) — are installed in the user environment (`~/.local/bin`, uv tools) and agents may invoke them directly, without delegation and despite being Python or third-party tools. This exception covers running those tools; it does not allow adding new `.py` files to the repo or wiring them into op-dbus services.
205|
206|All cargo commands run from repo root:
207|
208|**Owner decision (2026-10-17): JEV owns Cargo model selection and worker
209|routing.** Do not assign a Cargo-specific model, map caller families to models,
210|or wrap Cargo in another LLM dispatcher. Use JEV's existing routing without
211|model overrides. The primary agent stays available for source review,
212|decisions and user communication; execution workers run the assigned command

299|## Architecture — the load-bearing invariants (read these before touching plugins, state, or identity)
300|
301|- **Identity storage lifecycle (owner correction 2026-10-05).** Cozo owns identity-to-leaf/loop assignment and isolation. One immutable physical seed is shared through read-only views; each identity keeps its own writable leaf and the existing seven subvolumes. Only the external host provisioner may add a new blank leaf once, during explicit creation. Login, start, stop, logout, restart, bridge recovery and failed-start cleanup must NEVER add/remove Btrfs members. Start verifies/remounts the existing pair through the host mount owner; stop leaves membership and data intact. The bridge only verifies externally mounted storage and records logical attachment. Do not interpret `attached=false` as device removal. No root copies, snapshots, new subvolumes or OverlayFS fallback during identity provisioning. Never modify a seed while retained leaves depend on it. Older add-on-start/remove-on-stop guidance in source, handoffs and signals is superseded; do not restore it. Host release snapshot/send/receive below is a separate deployment mechanism.
302|- **D-Bus is the only control plane.** Every plugin is a D-Bus object at `/org/opdbus/v1/plugins/<name>` under `org.opdbus.v1`. No `Command::new(...)` subprocesses, no direct file reads for live state, no polling loops in plugin/service code. New backend capabilities register as plugins in `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs` — never as new gRPC proto service packages.
303|- **The plugin IS the schema — one source of truth, nonnegotiable.** That single schema is sealed into the blob, which IS the plugin. D-Bus method signatures, MCP tool inputs, gRPC shapes, and UI field renderers derive from it. Validate inputs against it. Each plugin defines its schema under `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`, using `plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs`. **There must be no parallel plugin schema source in a repository-level or plugin `schemas/` directory.** The former plugin capture directories, separate section files, and JSON-file loader have been removed. `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/schema_loader.rs` still exists by name, but it reads only a manifest-pinned `PluginSchema` from the sealed blob catalog; it is not a file-schema fallback. **Owner correction (2026-10-18): capture threetched's full `config schema` from the verified binary on every seal.** The shared capture fixes the runtime config directory, checks the binary and manifest, and supplies native_config, MCP, model_routes, plugins and skill_bundles. `tched_router_contract.rs` contains only access/section helpers; the embedded UPSTREAM IMPORT is retired. Build-time generated bridge contracts explicitly prepare the same capture; runtime consumes the sealed catalog and never starts capture as a fallback. Do not restore an embedded schema or add independent captures using the sealer's ambient environment. The per-section generator and generated surface were retired on 2026-10-04. Older docs claiming a single `plugin_schema_defs.rs` are also stale — that file does not exist.
304|- **The sealed blob IS the plugin.** Present state lives in the sealed blob catalog at `/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob`. A plugin exists ⟺ its blob is in the catalog. The sole writer is the blob sealer in `op-blob`. Consumers read SHM directly (zero-copy) — they never re-hash and never consult the Rust registry for existence. The old `/dev/shm/opdbus/schemas` folder and `live-schema.json` are gone.
305|- **MutationEngine owns state; streaming comes from SHM (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** MutationEngine folds authoritative backend results into the complete state tree, including child objects, and commits that state to canonical SHM before change notifications. Child updates/deletions must preserve unrelated children and parent fields. Existing subscriptions derive their values from committed SHM; an in-memory event payload, method argument, or generator buffer is not a second state authority. Preserve verified principal/session scope for private state. Do not add a separate per-method streaming control plane or claim a buffered unary response provides state streaming.
306|- **MCP gateway (settled).** One public MCP door: `:8090` on `op-grpc-bridge` (cognitive MCP is in-process there; no standalone `op-cognitive-mcp` runit service). `compact_mcp` is a retired plugin id. Compact *mode* (4 meta-tools) is in-process in op-web for the singleton control-plane chatbot; it is not an MCP plugin and not a second listener. Never create new shims or point external clients at `op-assistant-grpc`.
307|- **External binaries back plugins; the plugin remains the single schema source.** 3tched-router / tched-router (`tched_router` in code) is the framework/schema/plugin integration backed by the autonomous `/usr/bin/threetched` executable. The reproducible threetched input is pinned in `vendor/tched-router/source.pin`; `vendor/tched-router/build-threetched.sh` applies the checked-in patches and emits `target/threetched-artifacts/tched-router/{threetched,manifest.json}` without installing it. `build-golden.sh` validates the pin, patch and binary provenance, then stages the binary, `/usr/share/op-dbus/threetched-manifests/tched-router.json`, `/etc/op-dbus/threetched-runtime.toml`, and the tracked default skill bundle into the golden filesystem. The `tched-router` runit service verifies that manifest, exact commit, binary digest, and version before exec, then seeds its private runtime config and skills from those staged bootstrap files. A fresh checkout includes the digest-pinned upstream source archive, patches and build recipe; the helper verifies and uses that archive by default. Cargo registry dependencies and system build tools still need provisioning. Owner correction (2026-10-11): the executable and runtime-facing branding are lowercase `threetched`; the FUSE discovery source is `threetched-surface.rs`. Preserve upstream repository URLs, licenses and historical provenance. The former instruction to keep the executable named zeroclaw is superseded. The plugin contract remains `tched_router_contract.rs`, and source attribution may identify `zeroclaw config schema`.
308|- **Owner-confirmed lifecycle and model roles (2026-09-13, reaffirmed 2026-09-14).** Waypipe is retired: its crate directory, Cargo membership, binary target and protocol are absent; `retired-binaries`/`retired-services` prevent stale build or service artifacts from entering golden. Do not restore it in source exports or release inputs. Assistant is the control-plane chatbot, not an `assistant` container. The historical Gemma routing role is model agnostic; the `op-gemma` crate is retired (2026-09-19: directory, Cargo membership and binary removed, listed in `retired-binaries`) — the `gemma_brain` plugin remains and its role does not constrain the model/provider. Cargo membership and legacy names do not establish active deployments.
309|- **Factory role correction (2026-09-14).** The former Factory account/platform plugin is retired from the registry and dispatch. The intended access is CLI/SSH; routing belongs to `tched_router`, and Factory billing requires an actual native binding. Provider names or relabelled direct upstream routes do not prove that binding. A future Missions integration needs its own verified native contract; do not restore the retired REST platform methods from historical fixtures or docs.
310|- **Standalone vendor adapters are retired (2026-09-14).** The `op-grpc-adapters` crate directory and its `op.adapters.v1` protocol are absent after Netmaker retirement. Its duplicate mail/MQ services bypassed canonical plugin admission. Do not restore this crate or its old Netmaker clients. The existing bridge `operation.mail.v1` service and retained EMQX plugin are separate surfaces; their presence does not prove every mail or MQTT method is implemented.
311|- **Identity minting and metadata (owner reaffirmed 2026-09-13).** The identity subsystem owns minting the identity and its SealedId/SID1 credential blob. This is distinct from an OPBLOB01 plugin blob and does not belong in the plugin catalog. Clients forward the authored credential through the transport's identity metadata; they do not mint or reconstruct it from genesis/trace/key headers. Verify minting, persistence, injection and receiver validation as separate links. Current source assigns session/SID1 creation to MutationEngine with the op-identity format; the existence of an HTTP/MCP helper does not prove every gRPC client injects SID1.
312|- **Identity injection (owner decision 2026-09-25).** The decoy mints the sealed identity blob; the 8090 interceptor anchors the session and writes the identity metadata (`anchor_verified_human_session` and `insert_identity_metadata` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/interceptor.rs`). The oracle (OIA1) is the decoy's signed peer proof; the human credential (SID1) is the session identity for that key. The bridge's own client and MutationEngine are the wrong place for session or identity injection. Source and live state did not match this on 2026-09-25: the interceptor still mints genesis server-side when no session exists (`mint_and_store_genesis` in `anchor_verified_human_session`), and the decoy issuer mints only OIA1. Transport paths (decoy, WARP, door addresses) are in `docs/src/operations/network.md`.
313|- **Btrfs storage and transport (owner correction 2026-09-23).** Deployment remains the prepared snapshot transferred by `btrfs send/receive`. The earlier global five-subvolume limit and instruction to replace Snowball/cache subvolumes with ordinary directories are withdrawn. Preserve the original `operation-dbus-proto` cache/NUMA/timing architecture: Btrfs cache category subvolumes; authoritative timing plus vector/state subvolumes; aligned read-only snapshot sets and send/receive. See the original repo `branding/product-baseline.md` §12 and `crates/op-snowball/{DESIGN,REQUIREMENTS}.md` (R5). Retention is configurable per storage owner, not a global five-subvolume cap. Parent snapshots do not include nested subvolume contents: snapshot and transport every required member explicitly. Never flatten existing subvolumes or delete historical data to satisfy the withdrawn limit. Preserve security, writer-locking, identity and error-handling fixes while correcting storage regressions.
314|- **No SQLite — use CozoDB.** CozoDB (`op-cozo-store`) is the embedded database for this project. Do not add new `rusqlite` or other SQLite use. `op-cache/src/btrfs_cache.rs` already uses a Cozo index; current `workstack_cache.rs`, `workflow_cache.rs`, `workflow_tracker.rs`, and `pattern_tracker.rs` still use `rusqlite` and remain migration debt rather than an approved pattern.
315|- **RAG pipeline and Voyage-4 models.** Live source file indexing goes through `code_index` (mode='source') into Qdrant collections: `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_large` and `repos_lsp_*_voyage_4_lite`. Voyage-4 models are interchangeable across their dimension (1024 for all variants); `_large` and `_lite` refer to model size/quality tier, not embedding space. All collections share a single fused retrieval space and can be queried together. Legacy `repos_lsp_*_voyage_code_4` collections and `repomix_rag` collection are retired — do not use them. The standalone `notebooklm-mcp` service is retired; the plugin-owned `notebooklm` contract and bridge provider remain. Owner reaffirmed NotebookLM conversation/tool-history sync on 2026-10-05; use its declared methods through identity-bound 3tchedFS. Do not confuse this corpus sync with the Voyage source-indexing pipeline.

327|
328|- **Append observations to `SIGNALS.md`** rather than letting them evaporate in chat. Three signal types: `💡 SUGGESTION` · `⚠️ CONCERN` · `👁️ OBSERVATION`. Each row: date · model · signal · optional `→ OD-##` link. Models leave status `open`. Promote anything actionable to `WISHLIST.md` as an `OD-##` and link it back.

341|## Subagent and model selection
342|
343|Cargo execution follows JEV routing above; the guidance below does not allocate
344|Cargo models.

346|**Owner preference (2026-09-13, model names withdrawn 2026-09-24,
347|reaffirmed 2026-09-30): assess task
348|difficulty and required reasoning before delegation, and use the cheapest
349|available model that can complete it at the same quality.** A lower price must
350|not thin the answer, skip evidence, or weaken a judgment. If the cheaper model
351|would lose accuracy, completeness, or care, use the more capable model. Pick
352|from the models the session can actually launch. Do not inherit an expensive
353|parent model by default, and do not pin a product or model id in this file.
354|Use a low-cost model for lookups, inventory extraction, documentation
355|assembly and routine non-Cargo checks when that model can match the
356|quality of a more capable one. Choose low effort for mechanical work and

2|name: grpc-expert
3|description: "Expert guidance for gRPC/Protocol Buffers work in the operation-dbus-proto (OP-DBUS) workspace — designing plugin methods, generating .proto/service definitions, wiring the op-grpc-bridge, or fixing plugins with missing gRPC methods. Use this whenever the user mentions gRPC, proto/protobuf, plugin methods, the gRPC bridge, tonic, reflection descriptors, 'missing plugins' in the gRPC diagnostic page, or the seal/freeze/hot pipeline — even if they don't say 'gRPC' explicitly (e.g. 'the plugin isn't showing up on the diagnostic page', 'add a method to plugin X', 'regen protos')."
4|metadata:
5|  version: 1.0.0
6|disable-model-invocation: false
7|---
8|
9|# gRPC Expert — OP-DBUS
10|
11|This workspace does **not** hand-write per-plugin `.proto` files. Proto generation is
12|automatic, driven entirely by each plugin's `PluginSchema`. If you remember one thing
13|from this skill: **fixing a plugin's gRPC surface means editing its Rust schema
14|function, not writing `.proto`.**
15|
16|## The real pipeline (roll → seal → freeze → hot)
17|
18|```
19|1. Plugin declares  → PluginSchema { methods: HashMap<String, MethodDecl>, signals: Vec<SignalDecl>, ... }
20|                       in crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<plugin>.rs
21|2. Schema gets put   → op-projection's SchemaEngine publishes the catalog hash
22|                       (op_identity::schema_bridge::schema_catalog_hash())
23|3. Sealed by blob    → op-blob seals the plugin object into an immutable blob:
24|                       /dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/<plugin_id>.<schema_hash16>.blob
25|                       (op-blob is the ONLY writer — never write blobs elsewhere)
26|4. Descriptors       → TWO separate reflection layers exist, don't confuse them:
27|   for reflection       a) STATIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs generates
28|                            plugin_methods.proto from every plugin's schema.methods,
29|                            compiles it with tonic_build into operation_descriptor.bin
30|                            (a protobuf FileDescriptorSet), served by tonic-reflection.
31|                         b) DYNAMIC: crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/dynamic_reflection.rs
32|                            (ActiveReflectionCatalog) hydrates live from the sealed
33|                            SHM blob catalog via hydrate_reflection_from_shm() —
34|                            this is the "frozen" descriptor set for what's actually
35|                            present right now, independent of what's compiled in.
36|5. Frozen            → the blob + its descriptors are immutable once sealed.
37|6. gRPC socket = hot → crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs registers the
38|                       generated per-plugin service (plugin_method_routes.rs,
39|                       add_routes()) on the tonic UDS bridge, dispatching each
40|                       RPC to call_generated_plugin_method_typed(plugin_id,
41|                       schema_name, ...) which routes through PluginService.CallMethod
42|                       — i.e. gRPC never bypasses D-Bus, it's a bridge, not a
43|                       second control plane.
44|```
45|
46|A plugin shows green/connected on the gRPC diagnostic page **iff**:
47|- its `PluginSchema.methods` is non-empty (empty → `build.rs` silently skips it —
48|  see `collect_plugin_methods()`), **and**
49|- the plugin is sealed in the SHM blob catalog.
50|
51|These are discovery prerequisites, not proof of execution. Canonical dispatch
52|also requires the method's complete declaration and plugin version to match the
53|compiled handler, argument validation, verified identity, and its exact grant.
54|An advertised method whose adapter is absent is unfinished work.
55|
56|## Where to actually make changes
57|
58|| Task | File |
59||---|---|
60|| Add/fix methods for plugin `<name>` | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`, inside `<name>_schema()` |
61|| Reusable input/output builders | `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/plugin_scaffold_helpers.rs` |
62|| Regenerate the derived `.proto` + routes | Just rebuild — `build.rs` regenerates on every `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` (it `rerun-if-changed`s `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins`) |
63|| Wire a genuinely new (non-plugin-derived) service | `crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/*.proto`, add to the `compile_protos` list + `rerun-if-changed` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, then register in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/src/grpc_server.rs` |
64|| Inspect what's currently generated | `target/{debug,release}/build/op-grpc-bridge-*/out/plugin_methods.proto` (build artifact — never hand-edit) |
65|
66|**Never** create files under a `/proto/plugin_methods/` directory or a
67|`plugin_methods_unified.proto` by hand — those paths don't exist in this repo and
68|aren't part of the real pipeline; that was a stale spec from an earlier session.
69|The single source of truth is `schema.methods`.
70|
71|## Adding methods to a plugin (the actual workflow)
72|
73|Look at `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/proxy_server.rs` (`proxy_server_schema()`)
74|for the canonical pattern:
75|
76|```rust
77|use op_state_store::{MethodDecl, PluginSchema, SideEffect};
78|
79|schema.methods.insert(
80|    "start_proxy".to_string(),
81|    method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<StartProxyInput, plugin_scaffold_helpers::AckOutput>(
82|        "start_proxy",
83|        SideEffect::Mutation,       // Read | Mutation
84|        false,                       // idempotent?
85|        "cap.network.proxy.start@v1",   // required_capability
86|        "mut.network.proxy.start@v1",   // subid — must follow the taxonomy in CLAUDE.md
87|    ),
88|);
89|```
90|
91|- Define `StartProxyInput` (and a typed output struct, or reuse `AckOutput`) as
92|  `#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]` structs — the JSON Schema is derived, never
93|  hand-written as `serde_json::json!({...})` unless there's no existing helper.
94|- `method_decl_from_schemars_with_output::<Input, Output>` is the current
95|  (non-deprecated) helper; the single-generic `method_decl_from_schemars` is
96|  deprecated but still present for legacy callers.
97|- `subid` must be registered in the canonical registry per CLAUDE.md
98|  (`crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/oscal_subid_registry.rs`) — CI enforces
99|  uniqueness.
100|- For plugins with **zero** declared methods today (the ones missing from the
101|  diagnostic page), don't hand-author their methods one by one — see
102|  **The Auto-Creator Plugin** below. That's the actual deliverable: a plugin
103|  that finds these gaps and fills them itself, using real research per plugin.
104|
105|## The Auto-Creator Plugin (an ongoing capability, not a one-off batch)
106|
107|This is **not** a one-time task to fix ~11 named plugins. It's a standing
108|system capability: whenever the system encounters *any* missing plugin —
109|now, or a new one added in the future — it automatically generates that
110|plugin and submits it for **human review**, never auto-merges/auto-seals it
111|unreviewed. The current ~11 gaps are just the first real instances that
112|exercise this, not the scope.
113|
114|Consistent with this workspace's "reactive, not polled" principle (CLAUDE.md):
115|this should be triggered by an actual arrival/lookup that reveals the gap
116|(e.g. a D-Bus/gRPC call or reflection lookup against a plugin whose
117|`schema.methods` is empty, or a plugin name that doesn't resolve at all),
118|not a cron-style sweep re-scanning all plugins on a timer.
119|
120|Build it as a plugin itself (same `PluginSchema`/`MethodDecl` pattern as every
121|plugin in `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/`), whose job is to:
122|
123|1. **Detect a gap on encounter** — when something references a plugin that's
124|   missing or has `schema.methods.is_empty()` (same emptiness check
125|   `build.rs::collect_plugin_methods` already uses to skip plugins), that's
126|   the trigger — not a periodic scan of the whole registry.
127|2. **Research that specific gap** — drive deep research via the **NotebookLM
128|   MCP** (once wired up) to determine what capabilities/operations the
129|   missing plugin should realistically expose, given its existing state
130|   struct (if any), documentation, and prior art from comparable plugins
131|   already in the registry. This replaces guessing or generic Get/List/Watch
132|   stubs with a grounded, plugin-specific proposal.
133|3. **Synthesize typed schemas** — turn the research output into real Rust
134|   input/output structs (`#[derive(schemars::JsonSchema)]`) and `MethodDecl`
135|   entries — per the "no `AckOutput`" rule above, every synthesized method
136|   needs its own meaningful typed request/response, not a generic ack.
137|4. **Submit for human review — do not auto-apply.** The output is a proposed
138|   plugin/schema (e.g. a diff/PR against `<name>_schema()`, or a new
139|   `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs` for a wholly new plugin),
140|   held for a human to approve before it's merged. Only after human approval
141|   does it enter the normal pipeline (build → proto → reflection → sealed
142|   blob → hot). The auto-creator must never seal a blob or register a plugin
143|   into the live catalog on its own. It never emits `.proto` directly and
144|   never writes to `/proto/plugin_methods/` — the single source of truth
145|   stays `schema.methods`, authored by a human-approved change.
146|
147|In short: this is a **standing, reactive meta-plugin that drafts schemas for
148|whatever plugin is found missing, research-backed via NotebookLM, gated by
149|human review** — not a fixed batch job for a specific list of plugins.
150|
151|## JSON Schema → proto mapping
152|
153|The shared mapper lives in `crates/op-blob/src/json_schema_proto.rs`; the bridge
154|uses it for generated native messages. Structured objects become typed nested
155|messages; typed string-key maps retain their value types. Scalars preserve
156|presence, including explicit false, zero and empty strings. Unsigned 64-bit
157|contracts use `uint64`. Nulls, arbitrary JSON, unions and nested arrays use the
158|appropriate standard `Value`/`Struct`/`ListValue` dependencies. Arbitrary numbers
159|inside `Value` remain subject to protobuf's double-precision limit.
160|
161|Two existing wire layouts have distinct numbering rules: generated native
162|bridge fields use stable FNV-1a numbers; sealed per-method messages retain their
163|sorted sequential numbering. Preserve both layouts. Canonical schema map keys
164|and declared transport method names are separate identities, not interchangeable
165|aliases. Consumers register the original sealed descriptors and never reseal,
166|regenerate, or hash them as an existence check.
167|
168|## Known project-specific tensions vs. generic gRPC best practice
169|
170|Be aware of these before applying textbook advice unmodified:
171|
172|- **Do not use `AckOutput { success: bool }` for new/generated methods.**
173|  It exists in the codebase (see `proxy_server.rs`) as a legacy shortcut for
174|  "no meaningful return value," but every method a plugin exposes should have
175|  a real, dedicated typed **input** struct and typed **output** struct that
176|  reflect what the operation actually consumes and returns — not a generic
177|  bool. This matters especially for the auto-creator (below): when it
178|  synthesizes methods for a previously-empty plugin, it must generate a
179|  specific `<Method>Input` and `<Method>Output` schemars struct per method,
180|  never fall back to `AckOutput`. Errors still go through `tonic::Status` /
181|  D-Bus error replies, never a `success: false` field.
182|- **Enums are flattened to `string`, not real proto `enum`.** JSON Schema
183|  `enum` currently maps to proto `string` (see table above), so the classic
184|  `FOO_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED = 0` convention isn't applied by the generator today.
185|  If asked to add real proto enums, that requires changing
186|  `json_schema_type_to_proto` in `crates/op-grpc-bridge/build.rs`, not just the
187|  plugin schema.
188|- **Streaming comes from state in SHM.** The owner reaffirmed this on
189|  2026-09-13. Methods update authoritative SHM state before notifications;
190|  existing state subscriptions read that state. Current generated method RPCs
191|  being unary does not require another streaming method/service. Preserve
192|  private principal/session scope. Method arguments, event payloads and
193|  generator buffers are not independent state authorities, and buffered unary
194|  responses are not a substitute for SHM state streaming.
195|- **One generated file per bridge crate**, not the "1-1-1" file-per-message
196|  convention — `plugin_methods.proto` bundles every plugin's messages/services
197|  in one generated file. That's fine; it's a build artifact, not hand-maintained
198|  source, so the usual "small modular .proto files" guidance doesn't apply to it.
199|
200|## Generic protobuf/gRPC conventions (still apply to hand-written `.proto`)
201|
202|For any `.proto` you *do* hand-write (domain services under
203|`crates/op-grpc-bridge/proto/`, not plugin-derived ones):
204|
205|- `snake_case` field names, `CamelCase` message/service/RPC names, package names
206|  lowercase (this repo uses `operation.plugin.v1`-style packages).
207|- Reserve field numbers for removed fields; never reuse them.
208|- Prefer `optional` for fields that may be absent; avoid letting one field's
209|  value change the semantic meaning of another.
210|- Real proto `enum`s (where you control the generator, e.g. hand-written
211|  services) always start with `..._UNSPECIFIED = 0`.
212|- Use gRPC status codes (`tonic::Status`) for error paths; reserve response
213|  message fields for actual data.
214|- TLS is mandatory in this workspace (per CLAUDE.md zero-trust transport) —
215|  never wire a new gRPC service as plaintext, even over UDS.
216|- Server reflection (`tonic-reflection`) must stay wired for every new service
217|  so it's discoverable by `op-cognitive-mcp` and the gRPC diagnostic page —
218|  don't add a service that bypasses reflection registration.
219|
220|## Quick diagnostic checklist
221|
222|If a plugin isn't showing up / isn't callable over gRPC:
223|
224|1. Does `crates/op-plugins/src/state_plugins/<name>.rs`'s `<name>_schema()`
225|   actually populate `schema.methods`? (Empty → `build.rs` skips it entirely.)
226|2. Is the plugin registered via `inventory::submit! { PluginReg::new(...) }` in
227|   its own file (self-registration — check `crates/op-plugins/src/default_registry.rs`
228|   only if the plugin doesn't show up in `available_plugins()` at all)?
229|3. Did `cargo build -p op-grpc-bridge` actually rerun? (`build.rs` only reruns on
230|   changes under `../op-plugins/src/state_plugins` or `build.rs` itself.)
231|4. Is the plugin actually **sealed** in the SHM blob catalog
232|   (`/dev/shm/opdbus/plugin-blobs/`)? Static compiled-in proto support and the
233|   *dynamic* "hot" reflection/routing are two different gates — a plugin can
234|   compile fine and still be invisible if it was never sealed.","total_lines":234,"file_size":14428,"truncated":false,"is_binary":false,"is_image":false,"not_found":false}
